- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.5), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to account for volatility or reversal.
- Model consistently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days) — cap forecast rise to 3–4% after spike, then allow gradual mean reversion.
- If 3+ consecutive forecast days are above true outcome, apply downward correction by 0.5–1.5% per day to avoid overconfidence bias.
- If sentiment history shows strong reversal (e.g., +0.3 to -0.3 over 3 days), model often fails to adjust — add 0.5–1.0% downward bias to next forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate late-period (last 7–10 days) prices — increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for final 5–7 days if sentiment is neutral or positive.
